summary: 2D screening label: illustrative_2d_only (ThermoDSE, W7167828524, Table IV 'Ours' design). Thermal Studio did NOT run: simulation status is skipped because the input gate failed (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, but the floorplan and power_w are empty). input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, simulation_allowed=false, comparison_valid=false, independently_verified=false. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so it is steady-state only and has no transient trace. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes/powers or generated placement were supplied, so no input.flp or one-row input.ptrace exists and there is no source commit or placement assumption to report. The paper's reported peak temperature is 74.8 degC (Table IV, PDF page 10), under a 75 degC limit, from HotSpot 6.0 steady-state with 45 degC ambient and 0.4 K/W convection resistance. This is a paper-reported value only; there is no Studio temperature to compare against it. Any numerical comparison would require the same physical location, aggregation (chip-wide maximum), regime, and boundary assumptions, and these are not matched or even available. Only qualitative sensitivity can be discussed. Placement of high-power microtasks on corner cores, inter-chiplet spacing (2.3 mm), and the cooling boundary would be expected to influence peak temperature, but no quantitative claim follows. The gate controls the final verdict, so this is not a replication and no exact reproduction is claimed.

The packet has no pinned assets or paper-linked resources (artifact search found no links; assets list empty). No per-block coordinates, dimensions or power values are published for the selected design, so no complete floorplan or power input exists.

The paper models a 2.5D system with an interposer, BEOL layers, micro-bumps, a TIM/heat spreader/heat sink stack and distributed NoP power. A simple 2D steady-state Studio model cannot reproduce this stack or the interposer-level D2D heat coupling. Compute dies and an I/O die are separate, with ICS-dependent lateral coupling.

The paper's thermal result comes from workload-averaged component power from its own energy/latency simulator, with fine-grained task mapping. A one-row illustrative power trace has no equivalent of this, so the paper's workload-derived power distribution cannot be reproduced.
The optimizer (TED+SCBO) and design-space search are outside a thermal-solver runner. Only a single design point could be evaluated, not the DSE result.

No transient behavior, runtime controller or DVFS is modeled in the paper, which is steady-state only. Reliability and yield are modeled analytically, not thermally. This is a mismatch only if the Studio assumes transient dynamics.

3D stacking is explicitly out of scope (future work, PDF page 13). The cooling model is a fixed 0.4 K/W convection resistance with 45 C ambient and TESA-derived materials, which may differ from Studio defaults.
Any Studio run would be a separate illustrative 2D placement, not a replication of the paper's HotSpot 6.0 result.
Generated coordinates would be kept distinct from paper-derived facts, and any one-row power trace would be an assumption.

Studio package/material assumptions (die, interposer, TIM, spreader, heat sink properties and boundary conditions) are not extracted here. The paper does not publish its HotSpot material values, which are cited from TESA [12].
Studio temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's 74.8 C.
